newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Oct single-family home sales fell 8.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Oct single-family home sales fell 8.7 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department reported sales of new single-family homes, seasonally adjusted, with percent changes from prior months (numbers in 1,000s).
- Pct----Oct Sept--Rev from Aug--Rev from
-By Region: Pct----Oct Sept--Rev from Aug--Rev from
Total October sales of single-family homes rose 6.1 percent from an annualized rate of 673,000 units a year ago.
In 1,000s: Oct Sept--Rev from August--Rev from
Actual Units Sold 57 63 65 73 73
Note-Actual number of new single-family units sold is not seasonally adjusted.
Wall Street economists had expected October single-family home sales at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 772,000 units.
The department also revised monthly percent changes of total sales, seasonally adjusted, from prior months as follows:
- Sept-Rev from Aug--Rev from July--Rev from
The annualized sales rate for July was revised to 780,000 units from 785,000.
The department said the 8.7 percent drop in October single-family homes sales was the largest since the 9.1 percent fall in March.
The October supply of homes for sale rose to 5.6 months' worth from a revised 5.3 months' worth in September that was previously reported as 5.2 months.
The inventory of houses for sale at the end of October was 336,000 units, up from a revised 333,000 units in September that was previously reported as 336,000 units.
The department also said that the 32.3 percent decline in the Northeast region was the largest since the 33.6 percent drop in May of 1993.
The department said the 110,000 unit level in the Midwest region was the lowest since the 108,000 level in February 1995.
